item.title: GTA 6 Release: Nearly 1 in 5 US workers plan time off; 36% consider calling in sick
item.description: GTA 6's November 19 release has prompted workers across the United States to plan time off, with some even considering calling in sick. While Lander Allgood and Connor Folkers have arranged extended breaks to enjoy the game, others are choosing to wait until Thanksgiving. The launch has become a major event for gaming enthusiasts.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: US man accused of plotting foiled Hindu temple shooting in Illinois faces new charges
item.description: Alexandros Paporakis, a 19-year-old resident of Palatine, faces severe charges including terrorism and armed violence after allegedly planning a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple during the Navaratri festival. Reports from his co-workers contributed to his arrest, during which law enforcement discovered weapons and extremist propaganda. This incident has raised alarms within the Hindu community about escalating hate crimes.
item.dc:creator: Karan Manral

item.title: Palm Beach mansion linked to $194m CIA fraud sells for $24m after government seizure
item.description: In a stunning development, a lavish mansion in Palm Beach, Florida, has changed hands for $24 million. This opulent property was acquired using funds siphoned from a substantial government fraud scheme, orchestrated by the previous owner, David T. Nichols, who confessed to embezzling nearly $194 million. Following his conviction, authorities seized the estate, and the proceeds from this sale will aid in recovering the losses stemming from this extensive fraud.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian judge rejects son's inheritance claim but orders family firms to disclose financial records
item.description: In a recent legal dispute, a son faced a setback in his claims over family companies and property ownership. He believed his shareholder status gave him rights to specific assets within those firms. However, the court clarified that his view of shareholder entitlements was flawed, emphasizing that his rights pertained only to his investment. While his oppression claim was dismissed, he was permitted access to the company's financial documentation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Court reopens British mother's fight against daughter's adoption after her life turnaround
item.description: A British mother has begun to reclaim her life, overcoming a challenging past marked by substance abuse and domestic violence. Through psychotherapy, she has found stable housing and has maintained her sobriety. The Court of Appeal has given her a chance to contest the adoption of her daughter, previously denied by the Family Court, which deemed her progress still too recent.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida has secured roughly $5.2 million to protect nearly 830 acres across three farms
item.description: In a significant stride for land conservation, Florida's Commissioner of Agriculture, Wilton Simpson, revealed plans to safeguard three distinct properties spanning DeSoto, St. Johns, and Polk counties. These initiatives focus on sustaining agricultural lands while protecting valuable natural resources. Covering nearly 830 acres with diverse landscapes, including wetlands and forests, these easements are valued at over $5 million, allowing farmers to maintain their operations without land development.

item.title: Wrongful Death Lawsuit: Children sue over alleged faulty vent; claims unproven
item.description: In a tragic turn of events, three children are pursuing a wrongful death lawsuit following the passing of their parents, John and Kristen Ruskey, due to carbon monoxide poisoning on February 8, 2026, at their seaside home. The lawsuit claims that a faulty water heater and a malfunctioning carbon monoxide detector were significant factors in their untimely deaths.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Two brain regions tied to memory and emotion may shrink up a decade before Alzheimer’s symptoms
item.description: A groundbreaking study from Johns Hopkins University highlights early brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease. Specifically, it finds that tissue loss in the entorhinal cortex and amygdala occurs years before hippocampal changes manifest. The research suggests that abnormal tau protein accumulation may play a crucial role in this deterioration. Identifying these early changes could pave the way for timely interventions, enhancing future strategies for Alzheimer's prevention and treatment.

item.title: Court denies biological father parenthood rights after sexual assault finding
item.description: A Washington court ruled against a man's request for legal fatherhood of a child conceived through sexual assault. The ruling was based on Washington's Uniform Parentage Act, which addresses situations involving sexual violence. The child's mother provided credible evidence of ongoing abuse and intimidation from the man throughout their relationship. While the man claimed the relationship was consensual, the court found his testimony inconsistent and unconvincing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 1960 New Jersey home with wave-shaped roof lists for $1.65 million, studio for $995,000
item.description: Jules Gregory's Wave House in Lambertville has transitioned to condo status, now offering buyers the exciting option to purchase the main house, the separate studio, or both. The main residence boasts a distinctive architectural style with a generous open floor layout, while the studio presents a perfect solution for those desiring a cozy, minimalist living environment. This development allows prospective purchasers greater flexibility in selecting their ideal living arrangement.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: American couple turned a Volkswagen side hustle into a $30M hammock business
item.description: In 2011, Joe Demin and Rachel Connors embarked on a journey with Yellow Leaf Hammocks, originally as a side venture. Specializing in handwoven hammocks crafted by the Mlabri Tribe in Thailand, the couple faced a turning point during the pandemic. Post-Shark Tank, they pivoted to a direct-to-consumer model, empowering local women through training and crafting. Their dedication culminated in over $30 million in sales, profoundly impacting families.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Appeals Ruling: Court upholds $5,000 award; deck stays, unauthorised builds still carry costs
item.description: Moira and Denis Holden, a couple from Canada, constructed an unapproved wooden deck next to their cabin. They contested a demand from Valley's Edge Park Ltd. to have it taken down. The British Columbia Court of Appeal decided to uphold a $5,000 damages judgment, rather than requiring the deck's removal, as it found no notable adverse effects on the neighboring properties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Periodic radio bursts point to complex magnetic structure; source identity remains unresolved
item.description: Astronomers have made a remarkable discovery with a newly identified cosmic object, LPT J1555−5631, known for emitting intriguing radio pulses. This celestial entity produced bursts of radio waves over a span of 15 hours, then went silent for five years. Scientists are delving into its classification potential, considering various options like pulsars and magnetars, while the challenge lies in understanding its unique emission mechanisms and patterns.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Portland architect's flower-shaped forest home lists for $2.888 million
item.description: A unique forest home in Portland designed by architect Robert Oshatz is now listed at $2.888 million. The property features curved ceilings and disappearing glass walls that blend living space with nature. It includes four bedrooms, four bathrooms, and multiple levels accessible by an elevator. The home is part of a larger planned collection of residences sharing forested land.

item.title: Connecticut court upholds $62,530 award in employee's disability discrimination case
item.description: After colleagues reported a marijuana scent near her car, Latoya Council was fired from Charter Communications. Despite no evidence of her smoking or possessing marijuana at work, the ruling upheld by the Appellate Court pointed to bias against her PTSD condition. Following a protracted legal struggle, she secured compensation for her unjust termination, emphasizing the ongoing conflict between workplace regulations and the rights of those with disabilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Psychology says a few minutes of your speech may reveal how fast your brain is aging
item.description: A groundbreaking speech clock has been developed by researchers to evaluate speech patterns and estimate biological age. This innovative tool highlights the potential relationship between speech traits and cognitive decline, including dementia. Involving nearly 3,000 Spanish-speaking participants from various Latin American nations, the results suggest that noticeable differences in speech age may signal cognitive difficulties. Future research is essential to further explore the role of speech analysis in cognitive evaluations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Jeff Bridges leads US child-hunger campaign targeting 10 million children by 2032
item.description: Jeff Bridges is spearheading the Amplify Impact campaign aimed at eradicating child hunger across America. This ambitious initiative seeks to support 10 million children by 2032, highlighting innovative local solutions to the hunger crisis. Backed by a substantial $5 million in grants from No Kid Hungry, the campaign will fortify nutrition programs to ensure that every child has access to wholesome meals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
